title: Harsh Government Is Fiercer Than a Tiger
text:
Confucius was traveling past the side of Mount Tai with some of his disciples when he came upon a woman weeping bitterly beside a grave. He listened to her for a while, then sent his disciple Zilu to ask what had happened.

Zilu said to her that she wept like someone who had suffered sorrow upon sorrow. She told him it was so. Some years ago her husband's father had been killed by a tiger in this place. Then her husband had been killed by a tiger. And now her son had died the same way.

Confucius asked why she did not simply leave such a dangerous place. She answered: "Here there is no harsh government."

Confucius turned to his disciples and said: "Remember this, my children. Harsh government is fiercer than a tiger."
lesson: People will put up with real danger to escape constant oppression. If those you manage prefer hardship elsewhere to working under you, look at how you govern before you blame them.
